title: Machine learning identifies candidate sepsis molecular subtypes and associated markers
summary: Transcriptomic clustering and machine-learning feature selection identified three candidate sepsis groups with differing observed 28-day outcomes and a four-gene classifier. A separate dataset and cell experiments provide exploratory checks. The authors caution that these groups are not established clinical phenotypes and need prospective validation.
ai_technology: Nonnegative-matrix-factorization clustering defined transcriptomic groups; feature-selection methods and an SVM identified and classified subtype-associated markers.
organization: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Hospital of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Chengdu, China

evidence.tested: The classifier was assessed in a separate transcriptomic cohort; exploratory cell work examined one marker.
evidence.unknown: Subtype labels are not established clinical phenotypes; analysis and cell follow-up do not demonstrate clinical utility or treatment efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: Nonnegative-matrix-factorization clustering defined transcriptomic groups; feature-selection methods and an SVM identified and classified subtype-associated markers.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
